title: Breadcrumbs Ops - weekly notes (tracing, dashboards, cost telemetry)
content:
Week overview:

Quick summary: focused week on two parallel efforts — (A) trimming expensive high-cardinality spans from the default sampling set, and (B) reducing dashboard churn by batching tile refreshes and introducing cheap derived metrics for cost attribution. Small wins — p95 trace ingestion reduced ~9% in staging after sampling tweak; dashboard query load down ~18% with batched refresh. Still some unknowns around long-tail error attribution for archived models (see open questions).

Standup highlights (Mon-Fri):
- Mon 2027-11-15 09:30 — planning: agreed to roll sampling experiment v0.3 to staging; assigned metric hooks for cost attribution to Devon; set guardrail: revert if ingest reduction <5% or user-visible trace fidelity drops on our smoke prompts.
- Tue 2027-11-16 10:00 — experiment day 1: v0.3 sampling kicked off at 03:00UTC; observed 6.8% drop in spans ingested for hostnames matching "api-prod-*" and 11% on training jobs. Noted slight increase in span size for some long-run requests (investigating).
- Wed 2027-11-17 09:00 — dashboard refactor catch-up: Marta demoed the dashboard queueing patch (PR #678). Dev note: cache TTLs left at 30s for now, bump to 120s in next deploy if no regressions.
- Thu 2027-11-18 14:00 — cross-team sync with Platform: discussed fallback routing traces to cheaper S3 tier after 30d; legal flagged retention wording for EU customers (Priya to follow up).
- Fri 2027-11-19 11:00 — weekly retro: quantified ~18% reduction in query load on our main dashboards (observability-home, trace-explorer) after batching; agreed on next steps.

Measurements & quick numbers (staging / last 7d window):
- total spans ingested: -9.1% (v0.3 sampling vs baseline)
- average spans per request: -4.3%
- dashboard query volume (primary cluster): -18%
- p50 trace render time: -6%
- p95 trace render time: -2%
- estimated cost delta (infra): ~ -7% across tracing pipeline (still noisy)

Experiments & results:
1) Sampling v0.3 (hash-based + target-drop on high-cardinality keys)
   - What we changed: additional drop rules for session_id and device_id tags where cardinality > 100k; selective keep for errors and long-tail latencies > 2s.
   - Why: upstream storage & query costs spike from a small percentage of requests that generate thousands of unique span tags.
   - Result: ~9% ingestion reduction; key caveat — some rare error flows lost non-critical intermediate spans (we still capture error root spans).
   - Next: add an opaque sample-preserve token for replay when a downstream incident recreates a trace. Owner: Liam. Due: 2027-11-26.

2) Dashboard batching and derived metrics
   - What: group expensive tile refreshes into 60s buckets and precompute cheap derived metrics (token cost per-model, per-minute).
   - Result: dashboard cold-query count down 18%; average response latency yields smaller p95 improvement because big queries still run for deep traces.
   - Next: push derived metrics to a read-replica and experiment with 120s bucket. Owner: Marta. Due: 2027-11-25.

Runbook & playbook updates
- Added a small section to the tracing runbook about "sampling rollback criteria" and who to ping on-call for immediate revert (oncall-observability in Slack).
- Playbook link: confluence:Observability-Sampling-Playbook-2027 (needs copyediting).

Open questions / blockers
- Archived-model error attribution: our current cost telemetry pipeline drops model_version tag after 90 days due to cardinality concerns. How do we keep enough signal to attribute costs to archived models without reintroducing explosion? (Options: hashed model_version with bloom filter whitelist, or move full tags to cold storage with sample-preserve tokens). Action: Priya & Devon to prototype hashed attribution by 2027-11-30.
- Long-running trace size increase post-sampling tweak: observed in ~0.3% of requests we saw larger serialized span size — possible tagging duplication in proxy. Devon to correlate proxy logs with trace exporter. Blocker: lack of consistent request_id in proxy for older SDK versions.

Decisions made
- Adopt v0.3 sampling as default in staging for 2 weeks; revert if error debugability falls below baseline for at least one of our 5 monitor prompts.
- Move dashboard refresh batching to 60s for all non-critical dashboards.
- Keep retention policy unchanged for now; revisit after provenance for archived models is designed.

Action items (owner / due / status):
- Liam Chen: implement sample-preserve token + replay scaffold (due 2027-11-26) [in_progress]
- Marta Rossi: deploy derived metrics to read-replica; open follow-up PR to raise cache TTL to 120s if stable (due 2027-11-25) [in_progress]
- Devon Brooks: correlate proxy logs to trace exporter for inflating span sizes; create trace case examples (due 2027-11-23) [todo]
- Priya Nair: draft compliance-friendly proposal for archived-model attribution, include legal feedback (due 2027-11-30) [todo]
- Asha Patel (me): update runbook, add rollback checklist, schedule oncall run through (due 2027-11-22) [in_progress]

Meeting notes snippets (raw):
- "If we lose intermediate spans but keep error root + stack, is debugability practically impacted?" — short answer: depends on the engineer's workflow; for replayable incidents, root span + breadcrumbs are usually sufficient but long debugging sessions suffer. Need examples.
- Slack ref: #observability — see thread "sampling-v0.3-deploy" for heatmap + early screenshots.
- Jira: OBS-4123 = "sampling rules: add high-cardinality drop" (linked) — PR referenced above.

Notes to self / miscellaneous:
- Reminder: push small dashboard changes to canary cluster first; we saw one regression when I pushed the batching patch straight to prod in June 2027.
- Keep an eye on billing dashboard for the next 2 invoices, run a cost delta weekly snapshot.
- Could we add a small page in the Console that shows active sampling rate per-tenant? Nice UX for customers to understand why some traces missing. Feature request ticket: OBS-4190.

Risks / mitigations:
- Risk: over-aggressive sampling reduces signal needed for incidents. Mitigation: preserve error/long-tail spans + sample-preserve token for replay.
- Risk: derived metrics drift from raw data. Mitigation: keep nightly parity job and alert if delta > 3%.

Closing notes:
This felt like a productive week — good cross-team coordination with Platform & Legal. Priority next week: prototype hashed attribution for archived models, ship sample-preserve tokens, and iterate on dashboard TTLs.

-- end of notes --
